name: Skyways Air Services Ltd
title: Skyways Air Services Ltd - 544890 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Skyways Air Services Q2 FY27 revenue rose 90.3% YoY to Rs 1,311.45 crore, with PAT margin up to 2.53%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 1,311.45 crore, up 90.3% YoY and 7.8% QoQ, with H1 revenue of about Rs 2,528 crore, also up 90.3%. EBITDA rose 96% YoY to Rs 158.47 crore (the transcript also cites Rs 58.47 crore, which conflicts with the reported margin math), and PAT was Rs 33.18 crore in Q2 with a 2.53% margin. Growth was led by air cargo and ocean, with express and non-air businesses also growing. Management reiterated a target of over Rs 5,000 crore revenue for the full year and 25-30% annual volume growth over four to five years.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 158.47 crore as stated; Rs 58.47 crore also stated in the transcript, figures inconsistent
Rs 108.6 crore (stated as EBITDA; the CFO also called it EBITA)

financial_highlights.change: PAT margin +43 bps YoY as stated
PAT margin +46 bps YoY as stated

financial_highlights.value: Rs 4.5 per share (45% of Rs 10 face value as stated; 4% in transcript)

segments.name: Air cargo
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 983.4 crore, up 90.1% YoY; H1 Rs 1,997.9 crore, up 93.5%. Volumes 27,629 tonnes in Q2 (+27% YoY) and 51,115 tonnes in H1 (+25.2%).

segments.name: Ocean
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 247.1 crore, up 113.8% YoY; H1 Rs 399.72 crore, up 91.5%. Volumes 9,165 TEU in Q2 (+15.9%) and 17,187 TEU in H1 (+16.7%).

segments.name: Express and parcel
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 58.79 crore, up 34.6% YoY; H1 Rs 121.38 crore, up 48.2%. Shipments 72,197 in Q2 (+8.4%) and 134,967 in H1 (+17.7%).

segments.name: Non-air businesses (per Q&A)
segments.commentary: Non-air revenue cited at Rs 568 crore in H1 vs Rs 350 crore a year earlier, roughly 80-90% growth. Management did not give segment margins.

guidance_outlook: Full-year revenue target of over Rs 5,000 crore, with H2 expected to be similar to or better than H1.
Management expects 25-30% annual volume growth over the next four to five years.
Air freight yields expected to stay broadly stable barring fuel surcharge swings of 5-10% per quarter; larger shifts take three to four quarters.
Ocean rates expected to stay range-bound; normalisation expected over the next quarter or so as Middle East routing disruptions ease.
ASAP digital platform to launch in early Q4 FY27 after two to five weeks of final testing.
First of five new international geographies to be operational in Q4 FY27; remaining geographies over the next two to three quarters.
Target of gradual EBITDA margin improvement; new international offices targeted for early break-even versus the historical three to four years.
Import volumes expected to grow 40-42% this year; longer-term target of imports at 60-70% of the mix over four to five years (as stated in the Q&A).
capex_capacity: Cold chain facility in Delhi nearing completion, adding about 200,000 cubic feet of capacity for healthcare and food.
Warehouse operationalised in Birmingham, UK, targeting the automotive segment.
Further investment in a subsidiary to reduce its debt, and planned capital infusion into Page Root Logistic (rope freight, renewables; 76% stake held via a subsidiary).
Subsidiary being set up in a Freezone in Abu Dhabi to strengthen the Middle East presence.
Board approved expansion into five geographies (offices in Vietnam and Thailand already started); company remains asset-light and invests selectively in assets.
demand_pricing: Management said growth is about 3x the Indian export market (roughly 8% this quarter) and that Skyways remains the number one player in India.
Global ranking improved by two places to 42 at end-Q2.
Non-petroleum merchandise exports grew 18% to USD 259 billion (Apr-Oct); October merchandise exports were USD 49.47 billion vs USD 34.1 billion a year earlier (per management).
Air freight revenue per kg was cited by an analyst at about Rs 383; management said fuel surcharges drive quarterly variation of 5-10%.
Customer base steady at 9,500+; no customer losses reported.
Digital penetration: about 15-20% of overall bookings; express and e-commerce nearly 95-96% digital.
Revenue per employee up about 67% (90% revenue growth vs about 15% headcount growth, per management).

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise H1 performance vs H1 FY26, and margin breakup by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said air freight revenue rose almost 90% and ocean more than doubled (+116%), for 98% overall growth. It does not disclose segment-level margins, citing similar margin profiles across verticals.

qa_highlights.question: Why have ROE and ROCE declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the ROE decline to the denominator effect of pre-IPO and IPO equity; it said ROE would be about 16-16.5% on expanded equity and ROCE about 21-22%.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 5,000 crore revenue target be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 has historically been stronger than H1 over the last decade, and management expects H2 to match or beat H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins flat despite strong revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating leverage as employee and overhead costs fall as a share of revenue, with gradual margin improvement expected. It said the target is a PAT break-even for new offices and that net margins should beat asset-heavy peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timeline of ASAP, and its revenue expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Testing completes in two to five weeks and launch is in early Q4. Management expects to add 15-20% of business from tier 2-4 MSME markets via the platform, but gave no FY28 revenue figure.

qa_highlights.question: Export vs import mix and import growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Air imports rose from 2,500 tonnes (FY24) to 7,600 tonnes (FY26), with 40-42% import growth expected this year. Management targets a 60:40 to 70:30 mix in four to five years, which was not fully clear.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for the December quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a solid H2 and said Q4 is usually stronger than Q3, but gave no specific Q3 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on growth after the high base, and any slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management ruled out any degrowth and reiterated 25-30% annual volume growth over four to five years.

risks_watch: Internal inconsistencies in the transcript: Q2 EBITDA stated as both Rs 158.47 crore and Rs 58.47 crore; ROCE stated as 23% and 10.46%; dividend stated as 45% and 4% of face value. Verify against the filing.
ROE fell from about 22.37% to 14.15% (as cited by an analyst), with management attributing this to post-IPO equity dilution.
Ocean freight remains exposed to Middle East routing disruption and container repositioning; normalisation expected slowly.
Fuel surcharge-driven yield volatility of 5-10% per quarter could affect reported air revenue.
Execution risk on five new international offices, ASAP launch in Q4 FY27, and the Rs 5,000 crore full-year target.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on volume growth, the revenue target and the technology roadmap. Management was less precise on margins, segment profitability and figures, and gave no quantified guidance on margins or ASAP revenue.
key_quotes: We are growing at nearly three times.
This is not growth which has been concentrated just by one geography or by one customer segment or even one service line.
Ladies and gentlemen, each year, we are targeting a revenue of over 5,000 crores for this full year.

adds.what: Delhi cold chain facility adding about 200,000 cubic feet of capacity (healthcare and food)
Warehouse in Birmingham, UK targeting automotive segment
Subsidiary in Abu Dhabi Freezone for Middle East presence

growth.why: Management targets over Rs 5,000 crore FY27 revenue (H1 about Rs 2,528 crore, so H2 needs roughly Rs 2,470 crore+, similar to H1), plus 25-30% volume growth for 4-5 years, backed by partial specifics: Delhi cold chain (~200,000 cu ft), Birmingham warehouse, five new geographies, and an ASAP platform launch in early Q4 FY27, with no firm contracted capacity numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided gradual EBITDA margin improvement from operating leverage (employee and overhead costs falling as a share of revenue), though Q2 EBITDA margin is only 4.46% and the brief's EBITDA figures conflict.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Delhi cold chain (~200,000 cu ft) nearing completion, first of five new international geographies due Q4 FY27 and the rest over 2-3 quarters, though no capacity or capex figures were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided 25-30% annual volume growth; Q2 air volumes were up 27% YoY and H1 ocean TEU up 16.7%, and it ruled out degrowth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and no new capex amount was announced; the company describes itself as asset-light, with only selective asset investment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects H2 to match or beat H1 (H1 about Rs 2,528 crore) against a Rs 5,000 crore FY27 target, but it has not raised guidance and fuel surcharge swings of 5-10% per quarter add uncertainty.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The Rs 5,000 crore target needs H2 of about Rs 2,470 crore+, and ocean rates are range-bound with Middle East routing disruption, plus execution risk on five new offices and the ASAP launch.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ASAP digital platform launch in early Q4 FY27 after 2-5 weeks of testing, targeting 15-20% of business from tier 2-4 MSME markets, with no revenue figure given.

rows.label: Five new international geographies
rows.why: First geography operational in Q4 FY27 and the rest over the next 2-3 quarters, with offices in Vietnam and Thailand already started and an Abu Dhabi Freezone subsidiary planned.

rows.label: Import volume growth
rows.why: Management expects import volumes to grow 40-42% this year, following air imports rising from 2,500 tonnes (FY24) to 7,600 tonnes (FY26).

rows.label: Subsidiary debt reduction and Page Root capital infusion
rows.why: Management plans further investment in a subsidiary to reduce its debt and a capital infusion into Page Root Logistic (76% stake), with gross debt to equity at 0.58 as of 30 Sep 2026 and no amount disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume growth, the Rs 5,000 crore target and the ASAP launch, but vague on margins, segment profitability and ROCE. Analysts pushed on ROE decline, margin flatness, and the transcript's inconsistent EBITDA, ROCE and dividend figures.
